children.translated_text: Having heard the noble teaching and ascertained the ultimate truth (<s>pāramārthika tattva</s>),
seated on a soft cushion, with faith, the <s>yogī</s> should commence <s>yoga</s> (meditation).
'The apprehended (<s>grāhya</s>) and the apprehender (<s>grāhaka</s>), both, neither, I myself, <s>nirvṛti</s> (cessation), immersed' —
having discerned the net of manifold conceptual constructions (<s>vikalpa</s>), [there arises] mental absorption (<s>manaḥsamāpatti</s>).

children.text: jñeyaṃ vilokya sakalaṃ mā yogameva nirbhāsam /
children.translated_text: Having surveyed all that is to be known (<s>jñeya</s>), [one should see] nothing but <s>yoga</s> itself shining forth;
whatever is to be analyzed in the body, [one should pierce] with the <s>vajra</s> (thunderbolt) of <s>tathatā</s>-knowledge (suchness-knowledge).
Devoid of all aspects, free from the distinction of beginning and end, non-conceptual (<s>avikalpa</s>),
pervaded by a thousand stainless rays of light — everything becomes like the sky.
The mind (<s>citta</s>) sees what remains as merely its own form, itself primordially unarisen;
that by which it sees this, that too it perceives in just the same way.
That non-apprehension (<s>anupalambha</s>) is non-mind (<s>acitta</s>), <s>tathatā</s>-knowledge (suchness-knowledge), and the limit of reality (<s>bhūtakoṭi</s>);
thus, through practice regarding darkness, one attains the cessation known by <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom).
Endowed with these [qualities], the <s>yogī</s> performs the welfare of beings in manifold ways;
when this is perfected (<s>pariniṣpanna</s>), the <s>yogī</s> always abides on the noble path.
[...partially damaged...] ...by the winds of giving and density, immovable by the <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), <s>Māra</s>, and the rest;
[one should practice] the perfection of wisdom (<s>prajñāpāramitā</s>) always in this [state], for one who is constantly engaged.

body.translated_text: Many other [attainments] are also accomplished: <s>samādhi</s> (concentration), <s>yoga</s>, <s>dāna</s> (generosity), freedom from attachment, and the rest.
This is the work of the noble <s>Dignāga</s>.
